description: An eight-step, three-row sequencer whose row voltages are read a second time as gate probabilities, giving each row a gate output that fires at random in proportion to the step's value

params.text: Sets the rate of the internal clock, its value from -2 to 6 read as two to that power in hertz
Starts and stops the sequence; it comes up running
Sends the sequence back to the first step
Sets how many steps are played before the sequence returns to the first, 1 to 8
Sets the voltage this row's output carries while the sequence is on this step, 0-10V, and at the same time the chance that the row's P Gate output fires on it, none at 0 and certain at 10
Turns this step's gate on or off; the Gate output and this step's own Gate Out jack stay at 0V on a step turned off, while the row outputs carry their voltages either way
Bends the random number the row values are tested against: at -5 the draw collapses to the middle, at +5 it goes to one end or the other, at 0 it is even; the value is rounded to whole numbers

inputs.text: Added to the Clock knob before the rate is worked out, so one volt doubles the rate
Takes over the clock; each rising edge above 1V advances one step, and the Clock knob and Clock input are ignored while a cable is here
Added to the Reset button, and a total above 1V sends the sequence back to the first step
Added to the Steps knob at one step per volt, the total rounded and held between 1 and 8
Added to the Shape knob at one unit per volt, the total rounded and held between -5 and 5

outputs.text: 10V while the clock is high on a step whose gate button is on, and 0V otherwise
The voltage set by the first row's knob on the current step, 0-10V, held until the step changes
The voltage set by the second row's knob on the current step, 0-10V, held until the step changes
The voltage set by the third row's knob on the current step, 0-10V, held until the step changes
10V for as long as the clock is high when this row's knob on the current step beats a fresh random draw, and 0V when it loses
10V while the clock is high and the sequence is on this step with its gate button on, and 0V otherwise

notes: the sequence runs on its own clock as soon as the module is added; patch a clock to Ext Clk to take it over.
each P Gate output draws its own random number at every step, so the three rows fire independently of one another.
the draw happens once, at the moment the step changes; the P Gate output then stays at whatever it took until the clock goes low.
the gate buttons are toggles and their pattern is saved with the patch; randomising the module sets that pattern at random and leaves the knobs alone.
